package_info.why_malicious: The affected FortiOS SSL VPN firmware contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2024-21762) that allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code or commands via specially crafted HTTP requests. This enables full compromise of the device and potentially the network, making the affected firmware versions inherently dangerous until patched.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, upon receiving a specially crafted HTTP request to the SSL VPN web interface
execution_context.file_location: FortiOS SSL VPN web server component (proprietary binary, not open source)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: N/A (proprietary binary vulnerability; no source code disclosed. Exploitation involves sending a specially crafted HTTP request to the SSL VPN web interface, which triggers arbitrary code execution due to improper request handling in the binary.)
malicious_snippets.code_language: C (compiled firmware, exploit delivered via HTTP request)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the SSL VPN web server receives a specially crafted HTTP request, the vulnerable request parsing logic in the proprietary binary is triggered, allowing attacker-supplied code or commands to be executed on the device, resulting in remote code execution and full system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The vulnerability allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on the device simply by sending a crafted HTTP request, which is a critical security failure and never expected in secure firmware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, the SSL VPN web server should securely parse and validate all HTTP requests, ensuring that user input cannot influence code execution. In this case, attacker-controlled input is able to directly trigger arbitrary code execution, violating core security boundaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate scenario where unauthenticated remote code execution should be possible via the SSL VPN web interface. Only authenticated and authorized administrative actions should be permitted, and never arbitrary code execution.
key_indicators: Remote code execution triggered by unauthenticated HTTP request
Exploit targets proprietary SSL VPN web server binary
No authentication required for exploit to succeed
Abnormal or malformed HTTP requests to the SSL VPN interface
Unexpected process creation or command execution by the SSL VPN process

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request to the FortiOS SSL VPN web interface.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable code path in the SSL VPN web server binary is triggered, leading to arbitrary code or command execution on the device.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote code execution privileges on the FortiOS device.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full device compromise, enabling potential lateral movement, data exfiltration, or further network attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Inbound HTTP requests to the SSL VPN web interface with abnormal headers, payloads, or request structures
Unexpected process creation or command execution by the SSL VPN process following HTTP requests
Network connections initiated from the device to external or attacker-controlled infrastructure after receiving suspicious HTTP requests
file_indicators: Unexpected modification of system files or binaries on the FortiOS device
Creation of new files or scripts in system directories (e.g., /data/, /tmp/, /var/)
Presence of unauthorized scripts or binaries in system partitions
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with malformed or non-standard headers/payloads targeting the SSL VPN interface
Outbound connections from the device to unfamiliar or suspicious IP addresses or domains following such requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor FortiOS SSL VPN logs for anomalous or malformed HTTP requests, especially those that bypass normal authentication flows. Correlate these requests with subsequent unexpected process launches, file changes, or outbound network connections. Implement file integrity monitoring on system directories to detect unauthorized modifications. Apply vendor security patches immediately to mitigate the vulnerability.
